channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: White House Turmoil Erupts as Trump Axes Zacharia, Backs Wiles
item.description: Infighting gripping Donald Trump’s White House spilled into public view this week, with the abrupt exit of his hand-picked press secretary and the president forced to quash swirling questions about his chief of staff’s future.
item.dc:creator: Josh Wingrove and Hadriana Lowenkron

item.title: Scottish Nationalists Try to Get Independence Back on UK Agenda
item.description: Scottish First Minister John Swinney intensified his push for a second referendum on independence, countering Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s offer to work together and design a new model of regional empowerment.
item.dc:creator: Alastair Reed

item.title: Hungary to Unveil 2027 Budget Monday, Laying Out Euro Road Map
item.description: Hungary’s Prime Minister Peter Magyar said he would present the country’s 2027 budget in a speech to parliament at 1pm on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Escritt

item.title: Opposition Retains Czech Senate Control as Premier’s Party Slips
item.description: Control of the Czech Senate will remain in the hands of the current opposition after Prime Minister Andrej Babis’s ANO party lost ground in the upper house.
item.dc:creator: Michal Kubala

item.title: Republicans Brace For Backlash as Trump Gas Prices Near Biden’s
item.description: In his 2024 presidential campaign, Donald Trump made the cost of energy a centerpiece.
item.dc:creator: Kevin Crowley

item.title: Egypt Ready to Defend Saudi Arabia if Needed, Sisi Says
item.description: Egyptian President Abdel-Fattah El-Sisi said his nation stands ready to defend Saudi Arabia as it comes under attack from Yemen’s Houthis and called on parliament to convene an emergency session to authorize such action if it became necessary.
item.dc:creator: Tarek El-Tablawy

item.title: SpaceX Starlink Cuts Hobbled Ukraine Before Russian Bombardment
item.description: Restrictions on Ukraine’s use of SpaceX’s satellite technology came just weeks after its forces relied on the network for a surprising and successful counter-offensive that retook critical territory from Russian forces.
item.dc:creator: Ellen Milligan and Tony Capaccio

item.title: Houthis Hit Yemen Airport as Saudi Arabia Intercepts Attacks
item.description: Yemen’s Houthis struck the main airport in the nation’s interim capital on Friday, while its missiles and drones fired toward Saudi Arabia were intercepted, as the flare-up in fighting showed no sign of abating.
item.dc:creator: Sara Gharaibeh

item.title: Burnham Finds His Plans to Focus on Britain Blown Up by Trump
item.description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s bid to break from Keir Starmer’s premiership by focusing more on UK domestic policy and less on global events is proving near impossible in Donald Trump’s world.
item.dc:creator: Alex Wickham and Chloe Chaplain

item.title: Trump Halts New Russia Energy Sanctions to Ease Diesel Costs
item.description: President Donald Trump waived massive tariffs linked to Russian energy exports mandated in a law that he signed last month, as the measures complicated his push to lower diesel prices ahead of the US midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Alicia Diaz

item.title: Trump in Georgia Touts Manufacturing Gains as GOP Targets Ossoff
item.description: President Donald Trump touted his economic policies as bringing a manufacturing boom to Georgia as he sought to rally voters in a state hosting a crucial US Senate race in November’s midterm election.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Mason and Erik Wasson

item.title: Trump Says There's Zero Chance of Replacing Susie Wiles
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Mick Mulvaney, former acting White House Chief of Staff and Co-Founder of the Freedom Caucus, says the Trump administration “set” Katie Zacharia “up to fail” by not giving her enough preparation before she began her five-day tenure as White House press secretary. Suzanne Clark, President and CEO of the US Chamber of Commerce, says businesses want greater certainty, including faster permitting, more legal immigration, lower tariffs and additional trade agreements to open markets and make supply chains more consistent. Kendall Scudder, Texas Democratic party chair, says the party has built infrastructure it did not have in 2018, including recruiting more than 1,000 precinct chairs and coordinating candidates across the statewide ticket. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Scudder: Texas Democrats Are More Organized Than in 2018
item.description: Kendall Scudder, Texas Democratic party chair, says the party has built infrastructure it did not have in 2018, including recruiting more than 1,000 precinct chairs and coordinating candidates across the statewide ticket. Scudder says Democrats are also coming to the table with their own solutions rather than just pointing fingers at Republicans. He speaks with Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Clark Calls for Lower Tariffs, More Legal Immigration
item.description: Suzanne Clark, President and CEO of the US Chamber of Commerce, says businesses want greater certainty, including faster permitting, more legal immigration, lower tariffs and additional trade agreements to open markets and make supply chains more consistent. Clark says businesses are still seeing demand, but face labor shortages, particularly in construction and skilled trades. She speaks with Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AOC Boosts Abdul El-Sayed and 2028 Talk With $1 Million Check
item.description: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez said she was sending $1 million to Abdul El-Sayed’s campaign in Michigan, a key injection to boost his Senate bid and a signal of her ability to drive resources to progressives across the Democratic Party.
item.dc:creator: Derek Wallbank and Joshua Green

item.title: Mulvaney Says Katie Zacharia Was Set Up to Fail
item.description: Mick Mulvaney, former acting White House Chief of Staff and Co-Founder of the Freedom Caucus, says the Trump administration “set” Katie Zacharia “up to fail” by not giving her enough preparation before she began her five-day tenure as White House press secretary. Mulvaney says President Donald Trump does not necessarily need to quickly replace her and says whether Chief of Staff Susie Wiles remains in her role much longer is “anybody’s guess." He speaks with Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: David Rubenstein on New Book, “Speaking of America”
item.description: David Rubenstein, Co-Founder & Co-Chairman of Carlyle Group, has released two books in recent weeks: Inside the Owner’s Box, about the experience of owning a sports franchise, and Speaking of America, which brings 19 conversations he held with members of Congress at the Library of Congress into public view ahead of the midterm elections. He discusses the private setting encouraged Washington figures to speak more candidly than they would in public. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily Podcast: AI Jitters Persist
item.description:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF
Another burst of selling in technology companies rattled Wall Street on Friday, dragging down stocks as investors questioned the outlook for the artificial-intelligence trade. A rout in chipmakers extended into an eighth straight day on worries over whether the buildout of AI infrastructure has outrun the ability of firms to get a return on their investments. Meantime, Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh described AI as potentially the most consequential change to the US and global economy in his lifetime.
On today's episode: Mike McKee, Bloomberg News International Economics & Policy Correspondent Max Chafkin, Bloomberg Businessweek Senior Reporter Patrick McGee, Author of 'Apple in China: The Capture of the World's Greatest Company' Jason Leopold, Bloomberg News Senior Investigative Reporter (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Alberta Separation Referendum Draws Over 1 Million Early Votes in Canada
item.description: More than 1 million people have already cast their ballots in Alberta’s referendum on separation from Canada, signaling strong voter turnout that pollsters say may favor the “remain” side.
item.dc:creator: Iain Boekhoff and Derek Decloet

item.title: Trump’s New White House Press Secretary Out After Five Days
item.description: Katie Zacharia will no longer serve as President Donald Trump’s press secretary after spending less than a week on the job, thrusting the White House’s communications operation back into a state of chaos.
item.dc:creator: Josh Wingrove, Hadriana Lowenkron and Skylar Woodhouse
